subsystems.name: Entropy source
subsystems.role: the physical quantum process whose measurement outcome cannot be predicted even in principle.

subsystems.name: Detector front end
subsystems.role: turns single photons or field quadratures into electrical pulses.
parts: avalanche photodiode in Geiger mode (or superconducting nanowire detector)

subsystems.name: Digitisation and conditioning
subsystems.role: converts the analogue signal into raw bits and removes obvious bias.

subsystems.name: Randomness extractor
subsystems.role: compresses partially random raw bits into output that is provably close to uniform.

subsystems.name: Health monitoring
subsystems.role: detects a failing or tampered source before bad bits reach a key.

subsystems.name: Packaging and interface
subsystems.role: delivers bits to the system that needs them.
parts: chip, PCIe card or module housing

buildSteps.title: Pick the quantum process
buildSteps.detail: Choose a source whose unpredictability rests on quantum mechanics rather than on assumed computational hardness — photon arrival time at a beam splitter, vacuum field fluctuations, or phase noise in an interferometer.

buildSteps.title: Build the optical front end
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate the light path, either from discrete optical components or as an integrated photonic chip in silicon or similar material, aligning the source, splitter and detector paths.

buildSteps.title: Make the detector
buildSteps.detail: Operate an avalanche photodiode above its breakdown voltage so a single photon triggers a detectable avalanche, with active quenching to reset it quickly; superconducting nanowire detectors are used where higher speed and efficiency justify cryogenics.

buildSteps.title: Digitise the signal
buildSteps.detail: Amplify and compare or sample the detector output, converting each event into a raw bit, timestamp or multi-level value at rates from megabits to gigabits per second.

buildSteps.title: Condition the raw stream
buildSteps.detail: Measure the source's min-entropy and strip out bias and correlations, avoiding the trap of hashing away the very quantum noise being measured.

buildSteps.title: Run the extractor
buildSteps.detail: Apply a strong extractor such as Toeplitz hashing with a fresh random seed, so that even an adversary with partial knowledge of the raw output cannot predict the final bits.

buildSteps.title: Wrap in health testing
buildSteps.detail: Add continuous entropy estimation and statistical tests that run at every start-up and during operation, halting output if the source drifts or is disturbed.

buildSteps.title: Package and integrate
buildSteps.detail: Seal the unit as a chip, card or module, expose a clean interface, and embed it inside key-management hardware or a cloud service.

buildSteps.title: Validate independently
buildSteps.detail: Send the finished device to an accredited laboratory for entropy-source assessment against public criteria and statistical test suites before it is sold for security use.

prerequisites.why: avalanche photodiodes are a mature, mass-produced component; the whole device rests on detecting individual quantum events.
silicon and similar platforms allow the optics to shrink onto a chip, which is what turned QRNGs from lab benches into products.
decades of theoretical work on seeded extractors and hashing gives a proven way to turn noisy quantum data into uniform bits.

public criteria such as NIST SP 800-90B and Germany's AIS 31 exist, and ETSI has published a specification for quantum random number generators, but independent assessment of quantum sources is still maturing.
a device can only be trusted if the chip was built and kept without a hidden backdoor or side channel.

pathway.milestone: chip-scale generators sold inside hardware security modules, cloud key services and quantum key distribution equipment
pathway.unlocks: certified randomness where a flawed seed would undermine every key derived from it.

pathway.milestone: standardised, independently certified modules with published entropy evidence
pathway.unlocks: regulators and auditors accepting quantum entropy in high-assurance systems.

pathway.milestone: tight coupling with quantum key distribution networks and with post-quantum cryptography for key and seed generation
pathway.unlocks: end-to-end key material whose secrecy does not rest on an unproven hardness assumption.

pathway.milestone: device-independent generation, where randomness is certified by a Bell-inequality violation with no trust in the hardware at all
pathway.unlocks: randomness that can be trusted even if the device was built by an adversary.
